problem: Embodied scene representations either oversimplify geometry with discrete object-centric graphs or rely on dense 3D representations that are costly and incompatible with 2D-trained VLMs.
motivation: Embodied agents need a memory that supports spatial reasoning, exploration and long-term (lifelong) use. Multi-view 2D observations fit VLMs natively, but storing and retrieving them naively is costly.
key_idea: Use multi-view observations as memory primitives, organized by co-visibility into coherent views plus exploration frontier representations and retrieved by semantic guidance.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that grouping co-visible objects into views and retrieving selectively give memory compression (3.7x) and lower VLM inference time (68% reduction) while keeping accuracy.
method: Coherent View Representations: cluster co-visible objects into informative viewpoints used as memory units
Exploration Frontier Representations: unify reasoning and exploration by representing frontiers in the same memory
Semantic-Guided Retrieval: retrieve relevant memory entries guided by the query's semantics for efficient VLM access

setting.observation: multi-view egocentric RGB observations (details not given)

results: On Active Embodied Question Answering, CoViMem reaches 54.2% accuracy and 43.8% SPL, outperforming state-of-the-art VLM-based methods. It also gives 3.7x memory compression and a 68% reduction in VLM inference time.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details on the backbone, training, and baselines are unknown
Evaluation appears limited to Active EQA according to the abstract
